clue.text: Careless, contemptible sort of idiot losing ring

indicators.note: losing tells us the word for the idiot drops the letters given by the word ring

parts.note: a blithering idiot is a contemptible, utter fool, so blithering describes that sort
taken as written

explanation.surface: A careless person is dismissed as a contemptible idiot who has lost a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blithering idiot' is a stock British insult, so the adjective is the one the clue points to; 'losing' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe can mean casually heedless, a synonym of careless.

clue.text: A Rhine maiden learning to put on a garland

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: A Rhine maiden with an education puts on a garland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the legendary siren of the Rhine, a German river maiden.

clue.text: Enormous bird I can shift

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: shift tells us to move the letters of I can around

explanation.surface: A huge bird says it can move.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, like the Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Little animal with cold weather coming up keeping hot

indicators.note: keeping means the reversed pieces hold the letter for hot inside
coming up in a down clue means the words are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: and means with
ice is a sign of cold weather
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A small creature is out in freezing weather but keeps warm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'coming up' reads the pieces bottom to top, giving ECIDNA; 'keeping' puts the hot letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a small spiny anteater of Australia, an example of a little animal.

clue.text: Porter putting on coat appropriate for market

indicators.note: the beer is putting on the fur coat, so the coat word wraps round it

parts.note: sable is a prized fur, worn as a coat
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A railway porter dons his coat before heading to market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a railway worker, but it is the dark beer; 'putting on' means wearing, so the fur wraps the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something saleable is fit to be sold, so it is suitable for the market.

clue.text: As much as you can take of Latin

definitions.text: As much as you can take of Latin

parts.words: As much as you can take of Latin
parts.note: a Latin tag meaning to the point of sickness, and also how far you can tolerate Latin lessons

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means to a sickening degree, more than anyone can stand.

clue.text: Addresses of Roman college in the hills

definitions.meaning: cardinals of the Roman Catholic Sacred College are addressed as Your Eminence
an eminence is a raised piece of ground, a hill

explanation.definitionFit: Cardinals are styled Your Eminence, and eminences are also high places or hills.

clue.text: Mystify, showing grass unknown to the French

parts.note: bamboo is a giant grass
z is an unknown in algebra
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Grass that the French do not know baffles people.
explanation.definitionFit: To bamboozle is to trick or confuse someone, to mystify them.

clue.text: Stoical attitude which Shackleton took to the Antarctic

definitions.meaning: a stoic's patient bearing of hardship

definitions.text: which Shackleton took to the Antarctic
definitions.meaning: the name of the ship on Ernest Shackleton's 1914 expedition

explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is patient bearing of hardship, and it was also Shackleton's polar ship.

clue.text: Revolutionary's endless loyalty

indicators.note: endless tells us to cut the final letter from the word for loyalty

parts.note: troth is an old word for faithfulness or a pledged loyalty

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's loyalty never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter, H, from TROTH; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trot is the informal short name for a Trotskyist, a left-wing revolutionary.

clue.text: Like some spectacles given an edge by musician

parts.note: a horn is a horn player in an orchestra, a musician
something rimmed has been given an edge or border

explanation.surface: A musician gives some glasses an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Horn-rimmed glasses have frames made of horn or imitation horn, describing a style of spectacles.

clue.text: Levelled off, having gone up in aircraft

definitions.meaning: ... as in smoothed flat with a carpenter's plane

explanation.definitionFit: To plane wood is to level it off, and to plane is also to fly in an aircraft.

clue.text: Nice words for leavers

parts.note: Nice is the French city, so the words are the French farewell said to those departing

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is what someone in Nice says to people leaving: goodbye until we meet again.

clue.text: Hell! Ends of gable about to burn in fire

indicators.note: about to here means up against, so the ends of the gable sit next to the burning word

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and so hell itself
to char is to burn or scorch

indicators.note: ends of picks the first and last letters of the word gable

explanation.surface: Damn it, the gable ends are about to catch light in the blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: The gable's first and last letters, G and E, follow CHAR; 'about to' is read loosely as next to. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a gun is to fire it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Using two notes, write music? That's rot

parts.note: D is a musical note
E is another musical note
to compose is to write music

explanation.surface: A composer asks whether writing with just two notes is any good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's rot' looks like a verdict on the music, but rot is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To decompose is to decay, which is what rotting means.

clue.text: Shaft for flight giving way with, light wind — oh dear!

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
an air is a light breeze
well can be an exclamation of dismay, like oh dear

explanation.surface: Someone flying through a passage meets a gust and sighs in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' means a flight of stairs, not air travel; 'giving' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical space housing a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Meat and fibre in hamper

parts.note: ham is a cured meat
a string is a thin fibre or cord

explanation.surface: Meat and string are packed in a picnic hamper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a picnic basket, but here it is the verb to hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring someone is to cripple or hinder them, so it means hamper.

clue.text: Diner must change — these are basic principles

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of diner must are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner must alter their ways and go back to basics.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudiments are the first elements or fundamentals of a subject.

clue.text: Deceive member of family with speech

indicators.note: with speech tells us the relative's word is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a cousin is a member of the family

explanation.surface: Someone tricks a relative by talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To cozen is an old verb meaning to cheat or trick someone, so it means deceive.

clue.text: A speechless type, I accepted title

indicators.note: accepted means the shellfish takes the letter in, so it goes inside

parts.note: a clam is proverbially silent, as in to clam up

explanation.surface: A tongue-tied person admits to holding a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A title to property is a legal right to it, which is a claim.

clue.text: Crazy about a display of inlaid work

indicators.note: about tells us the word for crazy is turned round

parts.note: mad means crazy
a scene can be a showy display, as in making a scene

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about an exhibition of inlay.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene describes metal decorated with inlaid gold or silver, as made in Damascus.

clue.text: Relieved of place in crooked deal

indicators.note: in places the word for place inside the rearranged letters
crooked suggests the letters of deal are bent out of order

parts.note: to lay something is to put or place it

explanation.surface: Someone gets relief from their part in a dishonest deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges the letters of deal into ALED; 'in' sets the word for place inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Allayed means eased or calmed, as pain is relieved.

clue.text: Craft centre holding a class

indicators.note: holding means the word for centre wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: the core is the centre
CL is an abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: A craft centre is running a class.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat, a kind of craft.

clue.text: Offensive refusal is nothing to the writer

parts.note: no is a refusal
taken as written
O is zero, nothing
the writer refers to the setter, so me

explanation.surface: A writer finds a rude rejection means nothing to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or disgusting, that is offensive.

clue.text: Thirty-one days imprisonment I received at sea

indicators.note: received means the letter is taken in between the other two pieces

parts.note: March has thirty-one days, abbreviated Mar
doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A sailor gets a month in jail while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue was cut short in the text; the page continues 'I received at sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means relating to the sea, so it stands for at sea as an adjective phrase.

clue.text: Poet — not altogether a popular kind

indicators.note: not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poet who is not entirely popular or kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was an English poet, librarian at Hull, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Toed line by performing so?

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on an act and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: Someone toed the line by doing as told.
explanation.walkthrough: To toe the line is to do as you are told, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Toeing the line means conforming to rules, which is acting in a compliant, dutiful manner.

clue.text: Get rather rich, though reticent about source of loot

indicators.note: about places the shy word around the starting letter of loot

parts.note: coy means shy or reticent

indicators.note: source of picks the starting letter of the word loot

explanation.surface: Someone gets wealthy yet stays quiet about where the booty came from.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloy is to become sickly by being too rich or sweet, so getting rather rich in food.

clue.text: On Europe, German is on record as good speaker

parts.note: EU is the European Union
a log is a record, as in a ship's log
ist is the German word for is

explanation.surface: A German speaks well, putting Europe on the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogist delivers praise in a speech, a speaker who says good things.

clue.text: Bird on river to get more down

indicators.note: on in a down-style placing means the bird word comes after the river word

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A bird on the river gathers more down feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like feathers, but it means lower: to make deeper.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen is to go further down, getting more depth.
